direction: Compact dark decision cockpit based on the supplied dashboard reference
decisions: Management uses its own persisted theme preference and defaults to dark.
Mobile inventory navigation exposes Workbench, Receive, Issue, Inventory, and More.
Mobile management navigation exposes Overview, Sales, Inventory, Audience, and More.
Secondary modules live in bottom sheets so navigation remains readable at phone widths.
Motion remains feedback-only; POS, permission, inventory, and data contracts are unchanged.
The supplied Sunshine Health horizontal mark is used as a transparent, frameless brand asset across login, inventory, and management surfaces.
Desktop management uses a 100dvh application shell; navigation stays stable and long analytical content owns its internal overflow.
Motion is feedback-led: section context transitions, chart drawing, bar growth, loading indicators, restrained hover elevation, and mobile bottom-sheet transitions.
All motion honors prefers-reduced-motion and does not alter business state or delay operator actions.
Overview now uses a six-item compact metric strip, period-switchable sales trend, earnings-style expiry watch, inventory action rail, and Top 10 sales table.
At tablet and compact desktop widths, the left management navigation becomes one horizontal rail instead of wrapping into a tall, disordered card.
Overview period switches reuse the existing read-only sales-analysis API; no backend routes, write paths, or inventory facts were changed for the redesign.
Inventory reports now use a visible native date field; expiry review is a compact action queue with cumulative month filters, auditable batch-date correction, and manager-to-employee handling tasks.
Expiry alert rows expose separate Modify and Delete Alert controls; deletion requires a reason, preserves inventory facts, and is stored as an auditable soft hide.

Sales shortcuts now bind date range and aggregation dimension together; product stock alerts separate out-of-stock from threshold-based low stock and jump directly to the corresponding inventory filter.
Product analysis explicitly exposes incomplete POS mapping instead of presenting zero sales as a trustworthy business result.

Procurement uses one weekly order per store: suggestions, contextual add actions, editable draft lines, explicit confirmation and ordered states, while formal inventory remains unchanged until the existing receiving workflow is completed.
Replenishment suggestions expose 28-day sales, weekly velocity, current and target coverage; unsuitable rows can be ignored with a reason and restored without changing inventory.

Management density was tightened with compact headers, floating contextual help, six-column procurement cards, and a low-saturation blue-grey light theme; minimum-stock controls remain explicit operator actions.

Overview actions and product KPIs stay on one row at desktop widths; procurement cards use stronger theme-specific contrast, POS sync controls share one compact row, sales ranking amounts are legible in light mode, and procurement writes confirm through a one-second floating toast.
